title: React elements render purity reconciliation identity and keys
concepts: A React element is an immutable description of a UI node, not a DOM node; creating one does not display it.
Rendering calls components to calculate the next UI description. A render can be triggered without causing a DOM mutation.
React separates render calculation from commit work: it evaluates components, determines the required host changes, then applies relevant changes to the target renderer.
Render logic should be pure: the same props, state, and context produce the same result without changing pre-existing values. Events and Effects are separate places for side effects.
React models component relationships as a render tree, which differs from the host DOM tree and the JavaScript module dependency tree.
State belongs to a component identity at a position in the render tree. Type, position, and key determine whether React preserves that identity and its state across renders.

Keys identify siblings across list changes. Stable data-derived keys let React match moved or updated children; indexes and generated-on-render keys can associate state with the wrong item or reset it.
